maria: quick question — trying to capture a tiny nsys trace that isolates the KV cache hotpath for kernel selection experiments. any go-to minimal flags? :mag:

alex: for this use-case i usually do short captures with cuda + nvtx + osrt tracing and explicit capture-range via nvtx markers. keeps the file small and maps kernels to our code regions.

kevin: yup. something like:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=hotpath --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --duration=6s ./run_infer.sh
```
That grabs kernel timelines and OSRT markers. adjust duration to cover a few requests.

maria: nice. what about sampling vs full tracing? i remember sampling helps but misses short microkernels.

alex: right — sampling reduces overhead but can drop very short kernels (<~50us). if you're hunting per-kernel timeline and ordering, full cuda tracing is better for short spans. but file sizes blow up fast. tradeoff:
- sampling: good for long-running CPU stacks and coarse hotspots
- trace=cuda: required for exact kernel start/end and overlap

sam: another trick: capture bracketed NVTX around only the model forward loop so you don't record setup/teardown. e.g.
```
// pseudocode
nvtxRangePushA("infer_batch_start");
run_forward();
nvtxRangePop();
```
Then use `--capture-range=nvtx` so nsys only records between those markers.

kevin: also if you want kernel-level occupancy/SM stats use `nsys stats` after profile or enable `--stats=true`. can help identify weird kernel selection (e.g., small GEMM vs fused kernel choices).

maria: how long do you usually run the capture for kvcache eviction cases? the evict spikes are intermittent.

alex: for intermittent events i do bracketed runs around a synthetic workload that triggers eviction frequently, then run many short captures (3-8s) and compare. we label each run with `--output=evict-run-<n>` and keep a tiny scalar log to map runs -> config.

infra-bot: capture started: hotpath (1715000005) by maria

maria: sample command i used this morning:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=hotpath_v2 --capture-range=nvtx --duration=8s ./bench_kv_evict --batch-size=8 --seq=512
```
saw a ~2.3x tail in latency when kvcache swap happened.

kevin: if you want to correlate with batching heuristics, record request-level NVTX with batch size and sequence length inside your runtime. then in the timeline you can see which batch maps to which kernel launch.

alex: yea: `nvtxRangePushA("batch:8,seq:512")` right before dispatch. plot the timeline and check kernel name collisions and long gaps (GPU idle) — that points to host scheduling or async memcpy issues.

maria: any quick tips to keep the capture files manageable? gave up once file was 2.3GB.

sam: a few:
- bracket with NVTX to only capture the hot loop
- use `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` (don't add calls or memory unless you need them)
- reduce duration to smallest window that shows the issue
- run several short captures instead of one massive one
- post-process with `nsys stats` or `nsys export` to a smaller CSV for per-kernel rows

kevin: also check `--capture-range=pid` sometimes handy if you have one process doing the heavy work.

maria: when comparing two runs (baseline vs regressed), do you diff timelines or rely on aggregated stats?

alex: both. aggregated `nsys stats` gives quick diffs (kernel time, calls), but timeline diffs expose ordering/regression patterns like extra memcpy before GEMM or unexpected kernel fallback. i usually open both in the UI and scrub side-by-side, then export critical slices.

maria: any gotchas with OSRT sampling? last time i ran with `--trace=osrt` i saw probe noise that confused the timeline.

sam: OSRT markers are great for host-side scheduling visibility but they can add noise if you sample OSRT aggressively. recommended to combine OSRT traces with nvtx and use `--sample=none` for a pure timeline capture. if you need CPU stacks add sampling but expect more noise.

kevin: and watch out for drivers — different CUDA versions change kernel names/launch patterns. when we saw a perf regression last quarter, the kernel fused variant disappeared after a driver bump; timeline + stats made that obvious.

maria: perfect — i'm going to run 8 short captures with nvtx-bracketed runs and then post a couple of timeline screenshots. thanks :rocket:
